name: vendor.openwop.app-builder.workflows
description: The App Builder production chains (ADR 0346 / RFC 0013). The design chain is the portable source of truth for `app-builder.design` — the host registers it at boot via the feature's registration adapter (RFC 0124 deferred expansion), and it remains instantiable from the chain gallery like any chain.

chains.label: App design (PRD → research → plan → screens → audit → review)
chains.description: Design a multi-screen app from one idea: a concise PRD, grounded product research (personas, brand voice, visual direction), a screen-flow plan rendered into the closed `canvas.app-builder` component catalog, per-screen deepening of the thinnest screens, a deterministic quality audit, and a human review gate.

idea.description: The product idea to design an app for.

config.systemPrompt: You assess an app idea before design (AI-08). If the idea is materially ambiguous (unclear audience, contradictory scope, or a missing decision that would change the screens), reply with exactly one line starting with 'VERDICT_CLARIFY: ' followed by ONE focused question covering the most important unknowns. If the idea is clear enough to design, reply with exactly 'VERDICT_OK'. No other text.

config.question: The designer needs one clarification before building your app. See the question above and answer in a sentence or two.

schema.description: Your answer to the clarifying question.

config.systemPrompt: You are a product manager. Write a concise PRD (goals, target users, key user stories, screens list) for the app idea you are given. Markdown, under 500 words. If a 'clarifications' input is provided, treat it as the user's authoritative answers and honor it over any conflicting reading of the idea.

You are an app architect. From the PRD you are given, output ONLY a JSON object for the app design (raw JSON, no prose, no code fences): { "name", "description", "theme": "default", "themeColors": { "primary": "#rrggbb", "secondary": "#rrggbb" }, "screens": [{ "id", "name", "route", "isInitial", "x", "y", "components": [...] }], "connectors": [{ "from", "to", "trigger", "transition", "label" }] }. LAYOUT: give every screen integer "x" and "y" so the screens sit on a canvas in user-flow order — start the initial screen near x:80,y:80, space screens about 320 apart horizontally, wrap to a new row (about 520 lower) every 3–4 screens, keep values under ~4000, and never overlap. CONNECTORS: add one connector per navigation path with "from"/"to" screen ids, a "trigger" (click|submit|load), a "transition" (push|replace|modal|fade|slide|none), and a short "label"; leave sourceEdge/targetEdge unset (auto-routed). RESEARCH: you are also given product research (personas, brand voice, visual direction incl. suggested theme colors) — ground the copy, tone, and themeColors of every screen in it when present. CONTENT: use realistic, specific copy — real product names, labels, and plausible numbers — NEVER "Lorem ipsum" or placeholder text. Use ONLY these component types: stack, grid, card, accordion, tabs, dialog, drawer, spacer, heading, text, badge, chip, divider, alert, avatar, icon, progress, rating, calendar, snackbar, stepper, image, video, carousel, button, fab, textInput, textarea, dateInput, fileUpload, search, checkbox, toggle, select, radioGroup, slider, form (children: input controls, a submit button, and text/heading/divider/alert only), link, navBar (children: link/button only), sideNav (children: link/button/divider only), breadcrumb, pagination, list, table, statCard.

config.title: Review the app design
config.prompt: Review the generated screens — accept the design or send specific screens back for refinement.

report.description: The deterministic quality-audit report ({score, findings[]}) alongside the primary canvas.app-builder artifact.

chains.label: App Builder work plan → Kanban
chains.description: Turn an existing App Builder canvas into a reviewed, dependency-aware work plan on any selected Kanban board. The App Builder node only proposes work from the canvas; the reusable core Kanban node owns tenant scope, materialization, lifecycle and retries. Every node remains editable in the Workflow Builder.

canvasId.description: The stored canvas.app-builder design to plan.

boardId.description: The reusable Kanban board that will receive approved work-item projections.

columnId.description: Target board column id; defaults to todo.

workflowId.description: Optional workflow to attach to each proposed card; board-level trigger bindings remain editable separately.

config.title: Review the app work plan
config.prompt: Review the proposed screen work and dependencies. Approve to create tracked Kanban work; reject to edit the canvas or this workflow first.

workItems.description: The approved, durable core WorkItems created for this canvas revision.

cards.description: The board-card projections of the created WorkItems.

chains.label: App repair (governed: candidate → re-audit → review → apply)
chains.description: Repair an existing app design: read the current canvas, apply the repair instructions with one AI call re-normalized through the render gate, re-audit the candidate deterministically, review it at a human gate, and — only on approval — CAS-write it back as a new working-copy version (a concurrent edit conflicts, never clobbers).

instructions.description: What to repair — audit finding codes or a description.

config.title: Review the repaired design
config.prompt: Compare the repaired design against the findings — approve to apply it as a new version, or reject.

applied.description: { canvasId, newVersion } once the approved candidate is written.
